newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyotaru asks for protection from creditors.
newsitem.headline: Kyotaru asks for protection from creditors.

text.p: Kyotaru Co Ltd said it filed for protection from creditors with the Tokyo District Court on Sunday after racking up debts totalling 101.3 billion yen from losses in investments and poor business.

Shares of the company, listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE), will be under surveillance -- a formal procedure in which dealing authorities signal caution about particular shares -- from Monday, before being delisted from the exchange on April 20, the TSE said in a statement.
Kyotaru is a major restaurant chain operator based in Tokyo. Its mainline sushi take-out stores were hit hard by a food poisoning epidemic which swept the nation last summer.

The bursting of the 1980s "bubble" of inflated asset prices also dealt a heavy blow to the company's business. Kyotaru has been burdened with debts resulting from active investment in the United States and rapid expansion of its restaurant chain in Japan during the bubble era.

Kyotaru filed for court protection in order to restructure its operations under the Corporate Rehabilitation Law. Under the law, the assets of a financially strapped company are protected from creditors by the court if the court decides to proceed with the company's request for restructuring.

The company said it had assets worth 62.26 billion yen as of the end of October. Kyotaru, established in 1950 and employing just over 1,800 workers, plans to maintain normal operations from Monday, while streamlining operations at inefficient restaurants and divisions, Japanese newspapers reported.
